specification.problem: Density classification of binary inputs of length n=5 by a single-particle Quantum Particle Automaton (QPA): given x in {0,1}^5, the particle's state is evolved by a (genetic-algorithm-found) unitary U, the particle is measured, and the outcome's side of a boundary partition of the basis states decides whether x has majority 0 or majority 1.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest useful construction (chosen here as an assumption, since no experiment_scope was supplied): a single particle on a periodic 5-site line with a 2-level internal (coin/velocity) degree of freedom, a one-parameter theta step unitary applied T times, position measurement, and a fixed boundary partition of the 5 sites. The tiny explicit instance is n=5 with all 32 inputs (or the 30 inputs with at least one 1, depending on encoding), T=5 steps, partition B_1={3,4}, B_0={0,1,2}. Outside scope: the actual QPA definition of reference [12], the GA design and its search over unitaries/partitions, the specific unitaries found, the theta/mass analysis of solutions, and scaling to arbitrary n.

symbols.meaning: length of the binary input (fixed to 5 in the abstract)
binary input string whose density is to be classified
lattice site / position basis state of the particle; site j is identified with bit index j of x
parameter of the step unitary controlling the QPA dynamics (small theta: small mass, fast spreading)
number of evolution steps before measurement
initial particle state encoding input x
boundary partition of the position basis states into the 'decide 0' and 'decide 1' sides
probability that measurement collapses to the correct side of the partition for input x
GA fitness of a candidate (U, partition) pair

equations.label: Density classification target (majority)
equations.description: Classical target function: the automaton must output 1 iff more than half of the bits are 1. For n=5 the threshold is |x|>=3.
equations.abstract_quote: to decide if the binary input had majority density 0 or majority density 1
equations.justification: The abstract states the decision is majority density 0 vs 1 for inputs of length 5; this is the standard density classification task, and n=5 is odd so ties cannot occur.
assumptions: Density classification is the usual majority rule with no tie case for odd n.

equations.label: Input encoding into the initial particle state
equations.description: Assumed 'quantization' of the input: the particle is placed in a uniform superposition over the sites whose bit is 1, with the internal state initialized to |0>. The all-zero input has no valid encoding under this choice and is handled classically (trivially majority 0).
equations.justification: The abstract says the problem was quantized but does not state how the 5-bit input is mapped to a particle state; this is the simplest position-amplitude encoding consistent with 'basis states' on sites.
assumptions: Site j corresponds to bit j of x.
x=0^n is excluded or decided classically.

equations.label: One-step QPA unitary with parameter theta
equations.latex: U(\theta)=S\,(I_n\otimes C(\theta)),\quad C(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta & i\sin\theta\\ i\sin\theta & \cos\theta\end{pmatrix},\quad S=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}_n}\big(|j+1 \bmod n\rangle\langle j|\otimes|0\rangle\langle 0|_c+|j-1 \bmod n\rangle\langle j|\otimes|1\rangle\langle 1|_c\big)
equations.description: Assumed form of the QPA step: a theta-dependent internal mixing followed by a conditional shift on a periodic 5-site ring (indices reduced mod n). This is a one-particle quantum lattice-gas / coined-walk form in which theta plays the role of a mass-like parameter.
equations.justification: The abstract only says a particular parameter theta of the unitary drives the dynamics with small theta giving small mass and fast evolution; the explicit matrix of reference [12] and of the GA-found operators is not available, so a standard one-parameter single-particle lattice unitary is proposed. Position shifts are exact modular (periodic) reductions, not an assumed open boundary.
assumptions: Homogeneous, translation-invariant step with periodic boundary conditions.
Other GA-tunable parameters of U are suppressed; only theta is retained.

equations.label: QPA evolution for T steps
equations.description: The particle state after T applications of the step unitary.
equations.abstract_quote: the QPA needed a unitary operator to carry out the QPA evolution and a boundary partition to make the classification decisions
equations.justification: The abstract states that a unitary operator carries out the QPA evolution; repeated application for a fixed number of steps is the standard automaton semantics. The value of T is not given.
assumptions: A fixed number of steps T is applied; T=5 in the explicit instance.

equations.label: Boundary-partition decision and correct-side probability
equations.latex: p_j(x)=\sum_{c\in\{0,1\}}\big|\langle j,c|\psi_T(x)\rangle\big|^2,\qquad P_{\mathrm{corr}}(x)=\sum_{j\in B_{M(x)}}p_j(x),\qquad \hat{M}(x)=\begin{cases}1,&\text{measured }j\in B_1\\0,&\text{measured }j\in B_0\end{cases}
equations.description: The position is measured (internal state traced out); the outcome's side of the partition is the classification. P_corr is the probability of landing on the correct side; the classification is probabilistically correct if P_corr(x)>1/2.
equations.abstract_quote: when the particle was measured, it was more likely to collapse to the basis states that were on the correct side of the boundary partition
equations.justification: The abstract states the decision is made by which side of the boundary partition the measured basis state lies on, and that correct outcomes are 'more likely', i.e. P_corr(x)>1/2 rather than exactly 1.
assumptions: Only the position is used for the decision; the internal state is marginalized.
Partition is over position basis states; explicit instance B_1={3,4}, B_0={0,1,2}.

equations.label: GA fitness over all inputs
equations.description: Assumed fitness: mean correct-side probability over all encodable inputs; the GA maximizes F over unitary parameters and partitions.
equations.justification: The abstract says a GA searched for unitary operators and boundary partitions but does not state the fitness function; mean correct probability is a natural minimal choice. The actual GA encoding, operators, and fitness are unknown.
assumptions: Fitness is averaged uniformly over inputs.
An alternative (fraction of inputs with P_corr>1/2) is equally plausible.

registers.name: position
registers.size: 5 basis states (a 5-level qudit, or 3 qubits of which 5 computational basis states |0>..|4> are used)
registers.role: lattice site of the single particle; encodes input bits via eq_2 and is measured for the decision

registers.name: coin
registers.role: internal (velocity) degree of freedom mixed by C(theta) and controlling the shift direction

specification.initial_state: |psi_0(x)> = (1/sqrt(|x|)) sum_j x_j |j> (x) |0>_c, as in eq_2 (assumed encoding); for x=0^n the output 0 is returned classically.

steps.description: Classically compute the target label M(x) for each input x in X (used only for fitness/evaluation).
Prepare the particle's initial state from the binary input x on the position register with the coin in |0>.
Apply the theta-parameterized step unitary U(theta) (internal mixing then conditional periodic shift) T times.
Measure the position register; output 1 if the outcome lies in B_1 and 0 if it lies in B_0.
(Outer classical loop, out of circuit) Evaluate fitness over all inputs and let the GA search theta (and other unitary parameters) and the partition to maximize F.

specification.measurement: Projective measurement of the position register in the computational (site) basis after T steps; the coin register is not used (traced out). Repeated shots estimate p_j(x) and P_corr(x).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Map the measured site j to the label via the boundary partition (j in B_1 -> 1, j in B_0 -> 0); compare with M(x) to estimate P_corr(x) and compute the GA fitness F. The GA itself (selection, crossover, mutation over theta/U parameters and partitions) is classical and not specified by the abstract.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was given, so a single smallest construction (n=5, single particle, 2-level coin, periodic ring, T=5, partition B_1={3,4}) was chosen as the explicit instance.
The QPA of reference [12] is modeled as a homogeneous one-particle coined/lattice-gas unitary with a single mass-like parameter theta; the actual QPA definition may differ.
Input encoding (eq_2), number of steps T, and fitness (eq_6) are proposals, not taken from the paper.
Periodic boundary conditions (indices mod 5) are assumed for the shift.
missing_information: Exact definition of the Quantum Particle Automata of reference [12] (Hilbert space, update rule, role of theta).
How the binary input of length 5 is quantized into the initial particle state.
Explicit form and parametrization of the unitary operators searched and found by the GA, beyond the parameter theta.
Number of evolution steps before measurement.
Definition of the boundary partition found (which basis states lie on each side) and whether it partitions positions, internal states, or both.
GA details: chromosome encoding, fitness function, operators, population, and the reported accuracy of the found solutions.
Quantitative relation between theta and the effective particle mass/speed.
